title: Probe Maturity Model & Tenant Prioritization Canvas
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight planning canvas for standardizing "probes" (synthetic, session, and microprobes) across multi-tenant LLM inference. It combines a maturity model, a tenant-priority decision matrix, and a set of concrete metric/trace/dashboard contracts you can paste into PRs. Aim: reduce oncall noise, align SLIs to product impact, and make dashboard ownership explicit.

Context and problem statement:
- We ship many probe types across model rollouts, kv-cache experiments, and routing fallbacks. Operators see inconsistent naming, mismatched sampling, and dashboards with different aggregation levels.
- Result: alert fatigue, hard-to-reproduce regressions for tenants, and unclear remediation steps during bursts.

High-level outcomes we want:
1) Compact probe taxonomy that every feature roll or model onboarding follows.
2) Maturity model to decide what signals a feature needs before rollout.
3) Tenant prioritization matrix to allocate probe budget and trace sampling.
4) Reusable dashboard panel contracts + trace anchors for investigation.

Probe maturity model (levels):
- Level 0: Ad hoc logs only. No synthetic probe, manual ad-hoc queries in dashboards.
- Level 1: Probe baseline. One synthetic probe per user journey (p50/p95) + high-level counter metrics (requests, errors). Low sampling of traces.
- Level 2: Probes with cohorting. Add tenant slices (top N tenants + small/medium/long-tail). Traces collected for failures and outliers. Dashboards for warm/cold cache.
- Level 3: SLI-anchored probes. Each probe maps to an SLI + alert with runbook. Session reconstruction signals exist (session_id, prefix_warmth). Adaptive sampling based on tenant priority.
- Level 4: Auto-synthetic guardrails. Probes feed automated rollback/canary controls and are included in release gating; full trace snapshot for sampled incidents; replayable prompt context.

When to apply each level:
- Small experimental feature or spike: Level 0–1.
- Hosted API model migration for mid-market: Level 2.
- Dedicated/Private rollout or high-risk quality/regulatory feature: Level 3–4.

Tenant prioritization canvas (short):
Fields: tenant revenue tier, SLA tier, tenancy pattern (steady vs bursty), data-sensitivity (PHI/PII), historical volatility (past incidents), cache heat importance.
Scoring: each field 0–3, prioritize sampling & probe budget for tenants scoring >= 7.

Example scoring heuristic (quick):
- revenue tier: low=0, mid=1, high=3
- sla tier: self-serve=0, standard=1, enterprise=3
- burstiness: steady=0, occasional spikes=1, spiky=2
- data-sensitivity: none=0, low=1, regulated=3
- historical volatility: none=0, occasional=1, frequent=2
- cache heat importance: low=0, medium=1, critical=2

Operational decisions from score:
- score < 4: standard sampling (1%) and only level 1 probes
- 4–6: increased probe frequency (5%), tenant-aware dashboard slices, level 2 requirements
- >=7: priority sampling (10–20%), full-level-3 probes, faster trace retention for this tenant; alert escalation to SE/CS on incident

Metric & trace contracts (copyable block for PRs):
- Metric names: use kebab-case and prefix 'probe.' e.g., probe.synthetic.first-token-latency_ms, probe.synthetic.kv-warmth_score, probe.session.kv-cache-hit_rate
- Labels/tags: tenant_id, model_name, route, probe_name, sample_bucket (control/experiment), region
- Aggregation windows: define p50/p95/p99 buckets for latency; use 1m and 5m windows stored in short-term DB; 1h rollups for dashboards
- Trace anchor pattern: always set trace tags: trace.kind=probe, probe.name, tenant_id, request_id, kv_prefetch=true|false
- Error taxonomy for probe failures: probe_error.timeout, probe_error.kv_miss, probe_error.model_fallback, probe_error.response_parse

Dashboard panel contract (one-panels):
- Panel title pattern: <probe-name> — <tenant-cohort> — <primary-sli> (e.g., prefix-warmth — top-10-tenants — p95-latency)
- Minimum panels per probe:
  1) latency histogram (p50/95/99) with 1m/5m lines
  2) error rate with taxonomy breakdown
  3) kv-warmth / cache_hit_rate over time
  4) trace-sample list (links to trace UI) for top N recent errors
  5) tenant-weighted impact panel (tokens * request_count)
- Drilldown links: each panel must include link to associated runbook snippet + GitHub PR that introduced probe (if available)

Trace sampling policy (practical):
- Default sampling: 0.5% global for probes
- Tenant-priority override: up to 20% for high-priority tenants based on canvas score
- Failure and outlier sampling: always keep 100% traces for probe_error.* events triggered by probes for 30 minutes post-incident, then TTL to standard retention

Alerting & SLO mapping guidance:
- Keep primary alerts tied to SLI gaps not metric noise. Example: alert when probe.synthetic.first-token-latency_p95 > 500ms for 5m AND probe.synthetic.error_rate > 0.5%
- Use composite alerts where possible: e.g., p95 latency above threshold AND tenant-impact score > X to avoid paging on long-tail noise
- Escalation: page on level-3 tenants immediately; for lower tiers create ticket with severity mapped to tenant score

Instrument checklist (for engineers onboarding a probe):
1) Add metric names and labels per contract in PR
2) Wire probe to synthetic runner with stable probe_name
3) Add trace tags per anchor pattern and include request_id + seed prompt if possible (redact PHI)
4) Define dashboard panels using panel contract; reference panel in PR description
5) Add a short runbook snippet and expected remediation steps (cache warm, scale up model pool, rollback last deploy)
6) Set retention/sampling overrides for tenant if canvas score >=7

Runbook snippets (templated):
- Symptom: probe synthetic p95 > threshold
  Quick checks: model pool utilization, kv-eviction rate, network egress errors, recent rollout PRs.
  Action: trigger canary rollback if correlated with deploy; manually increase dedicated capacity for top tenants if throughput saturated; open incident for SE/CS if tenant flagged.

- Symptom: probe error taxonomy shows model_fallback spikes
  Quick checks: model artifact integrity, model variant mapping, routing policy fallbacks.
  Action: confirm if fallback was expected; if not, pin previous model variant and schedule investigation.

Ownership and review cadence:
- Probe owner: the feature or model team that introduced the probe (owner tag in metric)
- Dashboard owner: the team responsible for the feature (dashboard manifest in repo)
- Observability steward: eng-observability team owns the maturity model and sampling infra
- Review cadence: quarterly probe audit; rotating 2-week sprints where teams update probes tied to any active rollouts

Open questions & tradeoffs (for follow-up):
- What is the acceptable global trace budget? Sizing needed with infra (cost team).
- Automated promotion from level 2->3: what signal triggers it? Costs vs risk tradeoff.
- Tenant score weight tuning: initial heuristic above; needs validation against incident history.

Action items (next 6 weeks):
- (Owners: Maya + Priya) Create a lightweight probe linter (CI) that enforces metric/label contracts. Target: PR template by Mar 2026.
- (Owner: Liam) Build a tenant-score exporter that annotates tenant labels for sampling infra. Proof-of-concept by Feb 2026.
- (Owners: Observability + Product) Run a 2-week pilot with three Level-3 tenants to validate sampling and alert thresholds.
- Document a minimal runbook template and add it to the SDK quickstart.

Appendix: quick examples (copy to PRs)
1) Metric block to paste in code comments:
   probe.synthetic.first-token-latency_ms{tenant_id, model_name, route, probe_name, sample_bucket}
2) Trace tags example (JSON-ish):
   trace.tags = ["trace.kind:probe", "probe.name:kv-warmth-check", "tenant_id:acme-inc", "kv_prefetch:true"]

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally compact — meant to be a working canvas we iterate on. Looking for feedback on tenant scoring weights and a binary judgement on whether to require level-3 probes for Dedicated customers by default.

-- Maya
